project_title: PNIPAM Aggregation with a Multi-Chain Lattice Polymer Model

project_goal.primary: Extend the existing single-chain PNIPAM lattice model into a multi-chain model capable of studying collapse, aggregation, phase separation, and mesoglobule formation.
core_questions: Does single-chain collapse promote or suppress interchain aggregation?
Can the contact free energy fitted from single-chain REMD predict aggregation without additional fitting?
What additional physics is required to reproduce stable finite PNIPAM aggregates or mesoglobules?
project_goal.central_hypothesis: The fitted single-chain effective contact free energy can be transferred, as a first null model, to interchain contacts. Deviations from experiment will identify missing intermolecular physics.

current_single_chain_model.description: Self-avoiding lattice polymer with a temperature-dependent effective contact free energy.

existing_model_context.important_caution: The current molecular-to-lattice contact offset was fitted for single-chain intrachain contacts and must not be applied directly to interchain contacts.

system.box: Periodic cubic lattice with side length L
system.excluded_volume: At most one bead per lattice site
bead_metadata: optional bead type for later extensions

contacts.m_intra: Nonbonded nearest-neighbor contacts between beads on the same chain
contacts.m_inter: Nearest-neighbor contacts between beads on different chains
contacts.bonded_neighbor_rule: Covalently bonded neighbors are excluded from contact counts

baseline_hamiltonian.scientific_meaning: A monomer-monomer contact has the same effective free energy whether it is intrachain or interchain.

periodic_boundary_requirements.wrapped_coordinates: Used for occupancy, neighbor lookup, and contact counting.
periodic_boundary_requirements.unwrapped_coordinates: Used for per-chain radius of gyration and polymer geometry.
periodic_boundary_requirements.critical_validation: Chains crossing a periodic boundary must retain the correct Rg after unwrapping.

required_collective_moves.purpose: Allow translational diffusion and interchain encounters
Improve orientational sampling in dilute systems and near aggregate surfaces
Allow chains to rearrange inside dense clusters
Accelerate conformational equilibration in dilute or weakly collapsed regimes

equilibrium_vs_kinetics_rule.equilibrium: Nonlocal and replica-exchange moves are allowed.
equilibrium_vs_kinetics_rule.kinetics: Use only local or approximately diffusive moves. Do not interpret REMD, large pivots, or artificial cluster moves as physical kinetics.

replica_exchange.reason_for_general_rule: The Hamiltonian depends explicitly on temperature through g(T).
replica_exchange.swap_probability: p = min[1, exp(-beta_i H(X_j;T_i) - beta_j H(X_i;T_j) + beta_i H(X_i;T_i) + beta_j H(X_j;T_j))]
diagnostics: time spent in dispersed and aggregated states

chain_level: mean and distribution of per-chain Rg

cluster_level.definition: Each chain is a graph node. Two chains are connected when they share at least q_min interchain contacts.
observables: largest cluster fraction f_max = s_max / M

scattering.scientific_use: Separate single-chain contraction from collective concentration fluctuations and aggregation.

thermodynamics: heat capacity or energy fluctuation analog

initial_simulation_design.temperature_strategy: Start with the current REMD ladder, then add resolution near collapse and aggregation features.

pilot_experiment.main_question: Does the existing single-chain interaction produce a distinct aggregation transition in a multi-chain system?
pilot_experiment.success_criterion: The three controls clearly distinguish collapse-driven, aggregation-driven, and coupled behavior.

geometry_tests: bond length remains one lattice unit
detailed_balance_tests: incremental energy changes compared with full recomputation

limiting_cases.zero_interactions: Self-avoiding chains with only transient contacts
limiting_cases.g_inter_zero: Independent single-chain collapse without stable aggregation
limiting_cases.g_intra_zero: Interchain aggregation without intrinsic single-chain collapse
limiting_cases.strong_attraction: Dense aggregate formation with largest cluster approaching M

finite_size_scaling.procedure: Increase M and L together while holding N and phi fixed.
finite_size_scaling.mesoglobule_test: A characteristic finite aggregate size should become independent of total M and L at fixed concentration.
finite_size_scaling.phase_separation_signature: Aggregate size grows proportionally with total chain number.

possible_scenarios.aggregation_before_collapse: Expanded chains first form interchain bridges or loose clusters.
possible_scenarios.simultaneous: Collapse and aggregation are strongly coupled.

contact_motif_extension.research_question: Do specific bridge or junction motifs appear before conventional aggregation observables change?

add_when: single-chain collapse is reproduced but aggregation temperature is wrong
interchain contacts are systematically too strong or weak
aggregation is unusually sensitive to N
experimental end groups are charged or strongly hydrophilic
contact motifs disagree with molecular REMD
all systems collapse into one macroscopic aggregate
stable finite mesoglobules are the experimental target
temperature-dependent pair attraction cannot reproduce both collapse and aggregation
a more mechanistic PNIPAM LCST model is needed

research_roadmap.name: Specification and invariants
research_roadmap.objective: Define the exact statistical-mechanical model and the data structures needed for a multi-chain periodic system.
exit_criteria: model equations are fixed
all invariants are documented
expected energies and contact counts are known for unit tests

research_roadmap.name: Multi-chain geometry and moves
research_roadmap.objective: Create a correct multi-chain state representation and reversible Monte Carlo moves.
exit_criteria: no occupancy or connectivity failures
all move energy changes match full recomputation
chains diffuse in the zero-interaction limit

research_roadmap.name: Energy, REMD, and sampling validation
research_roadmap.objective: Implement temperature-dependent intra/interchain energies and correct replica exchange.
exit_criteria: manual swap tests pass
replicas make temperature round trips
energy histograms overlap sufficiently
known limiting behavior is reproduced

research_roadmap.name: Observables and cluster analysis
research_roadmap.objective: Measure single-chain collapse, interchain association, aggregate connectivity, and scattering.
exit_criteria: observables reproduce hand-designed examples
cluster definitions are robust to q_min
scattering code passes simple structure tests

research_roadmap.name: Three-control pilot
research_roadmap.objective: Determine how intrachain collapse and interchain attraction combine to produce aggregation.
tasks: compare order parameters and free-energy surfaces
exit_criteria: all controls equilibrate
collapse and aggregation signatures can be separated
the baseline model behavior is scientifically interpretable
deliverables: recommendation on whether separate interchain parameters are needed

research_roadmap.name: Concentration and chain-length mapping
research_roadmap.objective: Map how collapse and aggregation depend on N and phi/phi_star.
exit_criteria: transition lines are reproducible across seeds
concentration trends are statistically resolved
chain-length effects are quantified

research_roadmap.name: Finite-size and thermodynamic analysis
research_roadmap.objective: Distinguish finite-box condensation, macroscopic phase separation, and finite mesoglobules.
tasks: increase M and L at fixed N and phi
exit_criteria: finite-size trends are established
claims about phase transitions or mesoglobules are supported
finite-size artifacts are ruled out or explicitly identified

research_roadmap.name: PNIPAM-specific refinement
research_roadmap.objective: Add only the minimum additional physics required by discrepancies with experiment.
tasks: test separate interchain contact free energy
exit_criteria: each added parameter addresses a documented failure
model selection penalizes unnecessary complexity
new terms improve multiple observables rather than one curve

research_roadmap.name: Kinetic aggregation study
research_roadmap.objective: Study the structural sequence after a temperature quench without using unphysical equilibrium acceleration moves.
tasks: track Rg, m_inter, f_max, P(s), and motifs
compare collapse-first, aggregation-first, and simultaneous pathways
exit_criteria: multiple seeds show reproducible pathway classes
results are robust to local move probabilities
Monte Carlo time is not overinterpreted as physical time

no_aggregation: increase sampling before changing the Hamiltonian
aggregation_at_all_temperatures: check accidental application of contact offset
one_aggregate_always_forms: classify as phase separation unless finite aggregate size converges
collapse_and_aggregation_separate: map both transitions versus concentration and chain length

expected_major_results: A tested transferability criterion for single-chain contact energetics.
A collapse-aggregation phase map as a function of temperature, concentration, and chain length.
A thermodynamic distinction between finite clusters and macroscopic phase separation.
Identification of early multichain contact motifs that precede visible aggregation.
A justified hierarchy of PNIPAM-specific model extensions.
